MN202611_166u0a6lxos.t:
Wrexham sit 15th in the Championship table after 15 matches of the 2026-27 season

In the midst of a pivotal week for Wrexham , the club announced a shock shake-up within the boardroom.

Gone was chief executive officer Michael Williamson, back came director Shaun Harvey as acting CEO.

While change occurred off the pitch, Phil Parkinson steadied the ship on it.

Watching over were co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, who were in attendance for the 1-1 draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers, which came just shy of 24 hours after Williamson's exit.

Make no mistake, as Wrexham bid to achieve more success under their star owners, there is no doubt that recent changes at the Racecourse Ground have been immensely significant.

Wrexham toured in America in 2023, 2024 and 2026

From afar, Williamson's exit came as a surprise.

Williamson was appointed to the role of CEO just 34 days after Wrexham sealed promotion - at the time their second under Parkinson - into League One by thumping Forest Green Rovers 6-0 in north Wales.

The American - who previously worked at clubs including Inter Milan, DC United and Miami FC - oversaw huge growth as Wrexham evolved during their rise.

Overall staff numbers increased from 255 to 313 in his first year at the club, while Wrexham's iconic Racecourse Ground is also expanding.

Williamson had been a key figure in the development of Wrexham's new £69m Kop Stand, which is due to be completed next year.

He oversaw what was Wrexham's third successive promotion into the Championship - where the Red Dragons earned a highest-ever finish of seventh in 2025-26.

In November 2025, Williamson was named Football Industry Leader of the Year at the inaugural Global Football Industry Awards.

The club lauded Williamson for his pivotal role in the creation of the new academy facility at Darland High School, along with the subsequent approval of their English Football League (EFL) academy category three license.

The finances have continued to be boosted too.

Wrexham are expected to report a turnover of between £46m and £50m for the year ending June 2026, a huge jump on the £33.3m club record posted for their 2024-25 League One season , Williamson's first in north Wales.

But there has been growing discontent behind-the-scenes of late.

Wrexham claim point against in-form Wolves

Wrexham owners' presence uplifting - Parkinson

Wrexham made a key alteration to their transfer set-up in the summer.

Williamson took a prominent role in the club's transfer operations as director Harvey stepped down from day-to-day operations in early July.

Earlier this season, former Newcastle United chief Steve Nickson was appointed to the newly-created role of sporting director, a move welcomed by boss Parkinson . That said, he did not begin the role until after the summer window.

The transfer market proved difficult, as evidenced by the fact Wrexham were the last of the 24 Championship clubs to make a signing in the summer.

Two of their seven senior recruits - Callum O'Hare and Joe Worrall - joined on deadline day.

Only Danny Imray and Ben Whiteman arrived prior to the season opener against Middlesbrough in the League Cup on 7 August.

They were recently the subject of a bombshell announcement from the EFL regarding the registrations of summer signings O'Hare and Issa Kabore.

The club was fined £75,000 - of which £25,000 was suspended - after the EFL ruled that Kabore and O'Hare were ineligible to feature against Birmingham City and Millwall respectively earlier this season.

It led to the embarrassing situation of Southampton - who Wrexham mocked in the aftermath of the Spygate scandal - poking fun at the Red Dragons when they announced their line-up for the Sheffield United fixture in late October.

It was a game Wrexham went on to lose 1-0 following a lacklustre display, which led to Parkinson raising concerns over the performance of his players.

In the aftermath of the debacle, it was made clear the club want to recruit a new secretary - a vacancy that has existed since current club historian Geraint Parry stepped down from the role a year ago .

But the issues weren't simply behind-the-scenes. There have also been some concerns that the club has shown signs of losing its connection with supporters.

Changes to ticket policies in addition to the £10 surcharge - which was later scrapped due to a backlash from fans - required for supporters to use the Fanzone behind the temporary Kop stand in Williamson's first season at the club left the Wrexham faithful angered.

The club were also criticised in the summer for advertising merchandise featuring a white dragon, typically associated with England as opposed to the red dragon that features on the national flag of Wales.

It was seen as further evidence that the club's strong bond with those who have followed Wrexham through thick and thin has waned.

One beloved figure connected to the Red Dragons even told BBC Sport Wales that the achievements of some of the key members involved in Wrexham's rise have not been sufficiently recognised by some at the club.

Parkinson 'pleased' with point against Wolves

In a 139-word statement issued by Mac and Reynolds announcing Williamson's exit, the Hollywood pair wrote: "We remain focused on our most important task: to make the Wrexham community proud."

The word community was twice used in the brief statement. Plenty have made their own interpretations of the words chosen.

The announcement undoubtedly came out of the blue, with many staff on the ground in Wrexham only being made aware of the news shortly before the club's official announcement.

Parkinson himself was only informed on Friday morning prior to his pre-Wolves press conference, held at the club's Colliers Park training ground in the afternoon.

It was perhaps telling that Williamson's usual notes to fans were included in the Wolves matchday programme, despite his exit from the club a day earlier.

Only three days earlier, ahead of an impressive 2-0 victory against Middlesbrough, Williamson had utilised his programme notes to address the fiasco of Wrexham's breaches of player eligibility rules, incidents that occurred prior to sporting director Nickson's arrival.

"We co-operated with the EFL, carried out an internal review and have already taken steps to strengthen our processes and help prevent a recurrence," he wrote.

"As Wrexham AFC grows, our operations and infrastructure must keep pace with our ambitions on the pitch.

"Growth brings responsibility. We are proud of the progress being made, but we must be open and accountable when we fall short of our own standards. That is how we learn and build a stronger club for the long term."

Wrexham have largely operated in an efficient but ruthless fashion since being taken over by Reynolds and Mac in February 2021.

Icons including Paul Mullin, Elliot Lee, Andy Cannon, James McClean, Steven Fletcher and Ollie Palmer have all been moved on during the club's surge up the football pyramid.

Parkinson himself has been the recipient of some criticism during various stages of his five-and-a-half year tenure as boss.

The experienced manager rewarded the faith shown in him this week as his side collected four points in fixtures against two sides in Wolves and Boro that will likely be automatic promotion contenders come the latter stages of the campaign.

Williamson has not been as fortunate, and some of the reaction to his departure spoke volumes.

Former players Mullin, Lee, Cannon and Anthony Forde, along with Humphrey Ker - who recently stepped down as a director after five years with the club - were among those who liked a BBC Sport Wales post confirming Williamson's exit.

When one fan commented that those likes "says it all", former England midfielder Rob Lee - father of ex- Wrexham midfielder Elliot Lee - responded: "Yes it does."

Wrexham's acting CEO Shaun Harvey (right) is a long-time advisor to co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac

In Harvey, Wrexham feel they have someone who is more than just a safe pair of hands.

The 56-year-old has extensive knowledge of both the Welsh club and the English football structure following previous roles with Leeds United and Bradford City. He was also chief executive of the EFL between 2013 and 2019.

It is a huge part of the reason he has acted as an advisor to Reynolds and Mac ever since the duo became involved in the club.

Following his side's draw with Wolves, Parkinson said: "I had a brief chat with Shaun Harvey this morning.

"Shaun is back in a more official capacity, but he's always been around, he's been here since day one.

"He's an important figure. He understands everything about the club because he was one of the key people in starting off this journey with the owners."

There is clearly a strong bond between those at Wrexham and Harvey.

In the second minute of the contest with Wolves, Harvey headed to his seat in the Racecourse Ground's Macron Stand, known as the Mold Road Stand - the same stand in which Reynolds and Mac are situated for home games - and was roundly applauded by home fans.

The hope is that supporters will be continue to be applauding over the remaining months of the campaign.

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

Mac and Reynolds themselves stated Harvey has been an "integral part" of the club's journey.

Harvey could potentially land the role on a permanent basis, although an appointment would require approval from the Independent Football Regulator.

Nevertheless, it proved to be a seismic week for Wrexham.

The two-week international window will give those at the club a chance to take stock.

But the Championship grind will soon kick back in as Wrexham aim to build on their encouraging week on the field and continue their quest to clinch a play-off spot in just shy of six months' time.

"There's togetherness in the stands and with the boys on the pitch - but more than anything, there's just something about this place," the Deadpool star wrote on Instagram after the Wolves draw.

"Some of the best days of my life have been spent in this stadium, standing next to Rob Mac. Today was one of them. Up the Town."

Dormice across the South West will be going into hibernation in the coming weeks

Habitat work and a monitoring scheme have helped hazel dormice thrive at a National Trust site, despite declines elsewhere, experts have said.

Killerton National Trust has 100 nest boxes across its estate in Devon. Rangers weigh and record details of each mouse between April and October.

The trust said the animals "continue to thrive" in the area - a sign it was "doing something right" by creating a "healthy, diverse and well-connected habitat for wildlife".

The People's Trust for Endangered Species said populations had declined by over two thirds in the UK since 2000. Experts said the decline was largely down to "habitat fragmentation".

The mice start to hibernate when temperatures drop below about 10C (50F)

The trust hopes the mammals, which typically weigh between 20g and 40g, will have gained enough weight to begin hibernating in the coming weeks and survive the winter ahead.

Fi Hailstone, senior ranger for the National Trust at the Killerton estate, said: "When we have warmer weather, it wakes them up and when we have wet springs, that affects their ability to forage when they do wake up.

"So having a resilient ecosystem with lots of shelter for them, lots of scrub, lots of things for them to eat [is important]."

"They love bramble, and I know that bramble has a bit of a bad reputation with a lot of gardeners," Hailstone said.

"But bramble is the life source, really. It has flowers in the spring, it has berries on it. It's also protective in terms of cover from other predators, so it's a really great place for them to nest."

When they are not hibernating, they are shy and nocturnal.

Hailstone said Devon was "a bit of a stronghold for dormice" because "there is such a strong hedge network".

"We've been monitoring our dormouse population at Killerton since 2018, and during that time, we've noticed that they are fairly stable, which does buck national trends."

Hailstone said: "We are finding them in new areas which indicates them spreading across the estate.

"We think this is because we're planting a lot more hedges, a lot more trees."

Population numbers have declined since the turn of the century, but are currently stable in the Killerton estate area in Devon

"We might be planting lots of woodland now, which is great, but we won't see the effects of that for dormice for another 100 or so years," Hailstone added.

"It's really important to manage the woodlands that we already have in a positive way."

Anyone who finds a dormouse in the winter is urged not to pick it up but to alert the RSPCA or local animal shelter.

Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.

Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".

The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.

Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."

It came after the Sunday Times reported , external that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.

The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.

Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".

Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.

The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.

A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".

"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.

An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".

"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.

The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms.

YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures.

A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material".

That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites.

It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s. However, certain features such as its chat function will be restricted.

But Matthew Sinclair, a senior director at the Computer and Communications Industry Association, which represents tech companies, argued that ministers should prevent the rules having "scope creep".

He said a restriction on messaging for under-16s "would not stop at social media and would reach into the services families depend on to stay in touch", and urged the government to "ensure any new restrictions are proportionate and effective."

The UK's ban comes after a similar one was introduced in Australia last year.

Many children there have found ways to get round it, but the UK has said it intends to take a tougher approach.

In recent weeks, attention has turned to how a social media ban would be enforced.

Last month, the communications regulator Ofcom set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.

Rani Govender, head of online child safety at the NSPCC, said the "real question" going forward was how the government ensured age checks were effective.

"But effective age checks are only part of the solution," she added. "Tech companies must also be required to build child safety into every platform, device and AI tool, so children are protected from harmful and illegal content and only able to access age-appropriate services."

MN202611_16gmcmeba9w.t: In June, a father of two in Kimironko filed a case to Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) regarding a social commerce scam he had suffered after ordering and prepaying for commodities advertised on social media. He wanted to surprise his wife with a kitchen makeover after 10 years, and paid Rwf400,000 to an Instagram seller for household appliances that never arrived. The seller had supplied a delivery note, requested his personal details and promised to deliver a double-door refrigerator, gas cooker and juice maker. Then the seller disappeared. The appliances were advertised on an Instagram account using the name Smart Gulio, and the total purchase price was Rwf810,000. After negotiating with the seller, the buyer agreed to pay half upfront and the remaining Rwf410,000 upon delivery. He transferred the Rwf400,000 through mobile money to a recipient whose names were displayed as xxx. ALSO READ: How to outsmart mobile money scams The seller requested his name, telephone number and home address, reportedly to prepare electronic billing machine (EBM) invoices and arrange delivery. A delivery note followed, bearing an address in Muhanga. But the goods never arrived. Calls went unanswered, and the Instagram account was deleted. When the buyer asked a contact in Muhanga to verify the address, the person could not confirm it. He also contacted Smart Gulio, a Tanzanian electronics business whose product photographs appeared on the Instagram page. The company said it had no branch in Rwanda and was not working with anyone there. He had already sold his old refrigerator to make room for the new one. Instead of upgrading his kitchen, he was left without the appliances and facing the loss of his deposit. He reported the case to the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB). ALSO READ: Digital fraud in Rwanda declines below global average The case shows how vulnerable buyers can be when dealing with sellers who work online, and the need to establish safeguards in such space. Emmanuel Gatare, founder and managing director of Opus Digital, says the growth of social commerce has made it increasingly important for buyers to identify whom they are dealing with before sending money. Unlike established e-commerce platforms, which typically have processes for handling delivery problems and refunds, social media allows almost anyone to advertise products and direct prospective customers towards a payment method. “How credible is the resource?” Gatare asks, urging buyers to assess the credibility of a seller rather than accepting an online profile at face value. Philibert Murwanashyaka, co-founder and chief executive officer of Yali Labs, cautions that online reviews can also mislead buyers when they create an artificial impression of credibility. Gatare warns that online scams are evolving alongside artificial intelligence and other digital technologies, making some forms of deception harder to recognise. Deepfakes, for example, use fabricated audio or video to make people appear to say or do things they never did. Such material can exploit the trust people place in familiar faces and convincing visual evidence. Another technique involves manipulating company names, logos and typography to imitate established businesses. Small differences in spelling or presentation can escape notice, leading buyers to believe they are dealing with a genuine company. The same risk applies when fraudulent sellers copy product photographs from established retailers. In the Kimironko case, the buyer said he noticed a further inconsistency in photographs posted by the seller. “I noticed that the delivery van they posted had a steering wheel on the right, which is not common in Rwanda” he said. Gatare advises buyers to verify business addresses, confirm the seller's identity and establish whether the information provided about the business is consistent. Buyers purchasing from foreign sellers should consider established platforms rather than relying solely on social media accounts. Murwanashyaka warns buyers to be cautious when the business name on transaction documents differs from the name of the person or entity receiving the payment. “Although a mismatch does not automatically prove fraud, it should be explained before the transaction proceeds,” he said. He also identifies cryptocurrency payments as a serious warning sign in ordinary online shopping, particularly when a buyer is dealing with an unknown seller. “To me, if the seller asked to be paid in cryptocurrency, that is exactly a scam. You should never pay anyone you don’t know in cryptocurrency, no matter how legitimate you think they are,” he said. Figures presented by the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) on October 8 show that reported financial-sector fraud cases fell from 4,128 in the second quarter of 2025 to 2,879 in the same period of 2026, a decline of approximately 30.3 per cent. The amount of money involved decreased from Rwf637 million to Rwf471 million over the same period.

Rangers have won 10 and drawn two of their past 12 matches in all competitions

Rangers are unbeaten in their past 12 matches in all competitions, winning 10 of them, and moved to within a point of the Scottish Premiership summit after Saturday's 2-0 win away to St Mirren.

They thoroughly deserved their victory. They have the best defensive record in the top flight and the third best attacking record, but it feels as though they are not playing to their full potential.

In Paisley, Derek McInnes' side never quite put the game to bed despite a host of chances and St Mirren should really have pulled one back in the closing stages.

"There's still not that element of control," former Celtic striker Chris Sutton said on Sky Sports.

"That killer instinct is really important, but they don't control games the way they should. That will be the worry. Eventually that will bite Rangers in the backside."

Sutton's sparring partner on Sky - former Rangers and Scotland striker Kris Boyd - agreed.

"They are a good team, but with Rangers teams of the past, that would have been three or four," he said.

Rangers overcome St Mirren to move point behind Celtic

Ryan Naderi - who put Rangers in front from the penalty spot and has scored six in his past eight league matches - should have scored before he did.

Strike partner Kevin Kelsy missed a host of chances at the start of the second half before midfielder Dan Neil's deflected shot nestled in the bottom corner to make it 2-0.

Rangers' expected goals in their 12 league matches this season is 29.8. They have scored just 21.

Key striking duo Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland are both out injured and that goes some way to explaining their profligacy in front of goal, but it doesn't tell the full story.

Naderi and Kelsy have performed admirably this season - there have only been two matches since August in which neither man has scored.

It is the players behind them who have not fully stepped up to the plate.

South Korean winger Kim Min-su is yet to score or assist in Rangers colours since signing from Girona in the summer, although he created more chances than any other player on Saturday, while Badredine Bouanani has shown undoubted quality without regularly delivering end product.

Against St Mirren, there were plenty of promising attacking positions that did not result in a shot as players took the wrong option and allowed the home defence to recover.

As McInnes pointed out: "Loads of chances. It's quite ironic we scored from a penalty and a deflected shot, but some of our work was really clean up until the last part.

"What becomes a good chance could be a brilliant chance if we just take care with the weight of pass and make the right decision.

"There are umpteen examples in that game today and it's something we need to improve on. We've got to take ownership that we can do better in these moments.

"The top players make these decisions at breakneck speed and pick the right pass."

It is obviously something McInnes has impressed on his players and Neil referenced the need to be more ruthless.

"We speak all the time about being more clinical and there were a couple of chances we could have done better with," the former Sunderland midfielder said.

McInnes - who fell agonisingly short of winning the title with Heart of Midlothian last season - was open about how he wants and expects more from his players moving forwards, despite their impressive form.

"It's not been perfect," he said of the past two and a half months. "We've had the draw with Hearts and the draw at Dundee.

"Our fight is with ourselves to keep improving. If we can keep winning and getting those improvements as we go along, there's hopefully more to come from us."

If those improvements do come, Sutton believes Rangers could be hard to stop.

"They seem like a team that have another gear or two and that will be a worry for the other teams in the league," he added.

MN202611_eieijom282.t: The National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) is withdrawing selected old banknote series, specifically Rwf500, Rwf1,000, Rwf2,000 and Rwf5,000 notes issued between 2004 and 2015, while newer banknotes of the same denominations remain valid. The deadline for exchanging the affected notes was initially set for November 1, according to a public notice issued by the central bank. However, BNR recently extended it by one month, giving holders until November 30 to exchange the withdrawn notes through financial institutions. ALSO READ: Central bank extends deadline for exchanging old banknotes But what is the reason behind the withdrawal of such banknotes? One of the main reasons is that the central bank wants to strengthen currency security and reduce the number of different versions of the same denominations circulating in the country. Nicole Muhire, Director of Currency Operations at BNR, said the decision followed a review of banknotes in circulation, which identified older series that needed to be withdrawn. “The main purpose of this exercise is to remove some series of currency that have been in circulation for a long time and retain those with updated security features,” she said. She added that the move also seeks to reduce the risk of counterfeiting, although she noted that the level of counterfeit currency in Rwanda remains very low. She also pointed out that the current exercise does not involve issuing new banknotes. Rather, the central bank is removing older series and retaining more recent ones that already have updated security features. ALSO READ: How fraudsters distribute fake currency The banknotes being withdrawn are specific issues of four denominations. These include: Rwf500 notes issued on July 1, 2004, and January 1, 2013, Rwf1,000 notes issued on July 1, 2004, and May 1, 2015, Rwf2,000 notes issued on October 31, 2007 and Rwf5,000 notes issued on April 1, 2004, and February 1, 2009. According to the central bank, newer banknotes have enhanced security features, including a colour-changing security thread that shifts from green to blue depending on the angle at which the note is held. This distinguishes them from older series being withdrawn. The Rwf2,000 and Rwf5,000 notes introduced in June 2024 also feature wider, windowed security threads containing microtext with the letters “BNR” and their respective denominations. Their watermarks, displaying the National Coat of Arms and “BNR”, have been repositioned to the right-hand side. Why only banknotes? The current exercise concerns paper banknotes and does not include coins. Muhire said the central bank had prioritised banknotes for now, adding that coins could be considered for replacement in the future if a review establishes the need. She also dismissed suggestions that the withdrawal is connected to Rwanda's transition towards a cashless economy. “This is not related to the cashless economy. It is simply an exercise to clean up the banknotes in circulation, remove those that are vulnerable and retain particular series,” she said. From December 1 after the deadline elapses, holders of these particular notes will have to exchange the affected notes through BNR's designated facilities, with the overall exchange exercise scheduled to end on March 1 next year.

Arsenal's David Raya, Jordan Pickford of Everton and new Wales call-up Joe Duncan have all benefitted from non-league loans

David Raya had a loan spell at Southport before winning the Premier League with Arsenal, while Jordan Pickford spent time with Darlington and Alfreton Town on his way to a European Championship final and two World Cup semi-finals with England.

A non-league apprenticeship, it seems, can help a goalkeeper reach great heights.

That appeared to form part of Craig Bellamy's thinking when he announced his Wales squad for this month's Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal.

The one new name was Joe Duncan, a 20-year-old goalkeeper on loan at National League side Southend United from Bristol City.

Born in Bristol, Duncan was involved with Jamaica's youth set-up prior to committing to Wales, earning two under-21 caps before his surprise first call-up to the senior squad on Wednesday.

Wilson returns as Wales call up uncapped Duncan

His ascension to the higher echelons of the game has come sooner than expected, but he won't be thrown in for a debut in Oslo next weekend against Erling Haaland and company.

Instead, given Wales' dearth of goalkeeping options, Bellamy wants to take a closer look at some prospects for the future.

"You have to start somewhere as a goalkeeper, you have to learn your trade," the Wales head coach says.

"I love goalkeepers playing lower leagues, especially development goalkeepers, the ones who are looking to push through, because they [non-league players] are going to bump you and ask questions of you.

"Maybe you get over-protected the higher you go but, in those leagues, I think we quite enjoy watching those games because you're not getting anything. It's perfect, the way I see it, for a young goalkeeper.

"He's not someone who's always been on our radar because he hasn't been available to us. I have to be honest, everything I've seen with him at Southend, I really like."

It helps that Southend's manager is one of Bellamy's best friends from his playing days, former Newcastle and West Ham team-mate Kieron Dyer.

"Kieron loves [Duncan] and I respect his view on football," Bellamy says. "His IQ on the game is one of the best I've been involved with."

Bellamy has been to watch Duncan play for Southend but kept a low profile, so as not to distract the young keeper.

"That was the same week [England manager Thomas] Tuchel was watching PSG in the Champions League, so the world's different, but enjoyable," the ex-Wales captain grins.

Bellamy rummages further down the leagues than most of his international coaching peers because, quite simply, he has to. There's not much out there in terms of Welsh goalkeepers.

During his squad announcement on Wednesday, the former Liverpool and Manchester City forward described his current first-team regulars Karl Darlow, 36, and Danny Ward, 33, as "old".

It was a playful description, but his point was a serious one - where is Wales' next generation of keepers?

Everton reserve Tom King and Sheffield United's Adam Davies have usually been third choice behind Darlow and Ward but neither is playing for their club and, at 31 and 34 years old respectively, they are approaching the latter stages of their careers.

That means Bellamy has had to widen his search for successors. As he wryly notes himself, it is a far cry from Tuchel's situation with England, pondering whether to stick with Pickford or give another opportunity to Leeds United's James Trafford, who at 24 years old has already cost clubs nearly £100m in transfer fees.

Burnley paid a portion of that sum when Bellamy was working at Turf Moor as Vincent Kompany's assistant boss.

"You've got to earn your stripes. I've seen it with Traffs, who had really good loans with Bolton before he came to us," he says.

"We paid a lot of money for him but if we didn't do it then we were going to miss him."

Bellamy cannot delve into the transfer market to bolster Wales' goalkeeping ranks, which he describes as "an area where we're lacking at the moment".

What he can do is look far and wide – and sometimes in unexpected places – in his search for a future number one.

As Raya, Pickford, Trafford and others have shown, there is no shortage of examples to follow as Duncan plots his route to the top.

Umusatirizi wa Inter Miami, Lionel Messi, abaye umukinyi wa mbere mu mateka y'ihiganwa rya MLS (ry'imirwi y'umupira w'amaguru yo muri Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika na Canada) atahukanye ikirato c'inzahabu (Golden Boot) mu bihe bibiri vy'ihiganwa bikurikirana.

Messi, amaze no gutahukana agashimwe ka 'Ballon d'Or' incuro umunani, yinjije ibitsindo 26 mu nkino 31 yakinye. Arusha ibitsindo bine Peter Musa, umukinyi w'imbere wa FC Dallas, na bitanu Sam Surridge, umukinyi w'imbere w'Umwongereza akinira Nashville.

Messi abaye umukinyi agira gatandatu atahukanye ako gashimwe incuro zibiri. Agiye ku rutonde rw'abandi bakinyi harimwo Bradley Wright-Phillips yahoze akinira imirwi ya Charlton Athletic na Southampton.

Uretse ibitsindo yinjije, uwo mukinyi w'imyaka 39 yatanze kandi imipira 17 yavuyemwo ibitsindo mu nkino zose z'ihiganwa rya MLS. Ivyo vyatumye agira uruhara mu bitsindo 43, biciye mu kwinjiza ibitsindo no gufasha abandi kuvyinjiza, aca aba umukinyi wa mbere mwiza ku mwaka ugira kabiri yikurikirana.

Uwo yatwaye igikombe c'isi, arashobora kandi kwandika ayandi mateka mu gihe ariko arondera kuba umukinyi wa mbere atahukanye incuro zitatu agashimwe ka Landon Donovan MLS MVP, gahabwa uwigenjeje neza kurusha abandi muri MLS.

Messi yahoze akinira umurwi nserukiragihugu wa Argentine yatwaye ako gashimwe mu 2024, igihe Inter Miami yatahukana igikombe ca Supporters' Shield, yongera kukegukana mu 2025, igihe uwo murwi watwara igikombe ca MLS Cup.

N'ubwo yerekanye ubuhinga budasanzwe, Inter Miami ntiyashoboye kurangiza ihiganwa iri mu kibanza ca mbere mu karere ka Eastern Conference ka MLS. Uwo murwi warangije urushwa amanota 17 na Nashville ya Surridge.

Ubu Inter Miami igiye gukina na Columbus Crew mu nkino zitatu zo mu gice ca mbere c'ihiganwa ryo kurondera igikombe ca MLS Cup, zizotangura inyuma y'uku kwezi.

Muhanga: Inzego z’Ubugenzacyaha n’iz’Umutekano zataye muri yombi Iradukunda Emmanuel zimukekaho kwica Nyirakuru ubyara Se ufite imyaka 86 y’amavuko.

Byabereye mu Mudugudu wa Cyubutare, Akagari ka Nyamirama, Umurenge wa Muhanga.

Gitifu w’Umurenge wa Muhanga, Musabwa Aimable yabwiye UMUSEKE ko amakuru bamenye avuga ko uyu Iradukunda Emmanuel w’imyaka 22 yagiye kwa Nyirakuru saa mbili z’ijoro, yitwaje umuhoro ahageze aramutema.

Ati: “Yacunze mukuru we usanzwe abana na Nyirakuru adahari, Iradukunda ajya kwica uyu mukecuru.”

Gitifu Musabwa avuga ko bahawe amakuru n’abaturage ko Iradukunda yajyaga gutema ibiti byo mu ishyamba rya Nyirakuru akabyifashisha atwika amakara, biza kurakaza Nyirakuru Nakabonye Anastasie kugeza ubwo yashyikirije ikirego Inzego z’Ubuyobozi uyu musore agenza makeya ntiyaba akijya muri iryo shyamba, ariko akomeza kubika inzika kugeza ubwo afashe iki cyemezo cyo kuvutsa ubuzima Nyirakuru.

Musabwa yavuze ko Iradukunda amaze gukora ibi, yagerageje gucika bamufatira ahagana mu Murenge wa Nyarusange.

Bamwe mu baturage babwiye UMUSEKE ko Iradukunda yishe Nyirakuru urupfu rubabaje.

Ubuyobozi bw’Umurenge buvuga ko uyu mukuru we wabanaga na Nyirakuru bamutabaje ibi bikimara kuba ababwira ko yaraye mu birombe, kuko avugwa mu bakora ubucukuzi bw’amabuye y’agaciro butemewe, abo bakunze kwita (abahebyi).

Ubuyobozi bukavuga ko iyo ajya kuba ari kumwe n’uyu mukecuru murumana we atari gutinyuka ngo amuvutse ubuzima.

Gitifu Musabwa avuga ko Inzego z’Ubugenzacyaha, iz’ibanze ndetse na Polisi bahageze, RIB ikaba yatangiye gukora iperereza.

Umurambo wa Nakabonye Anastasie uracyari muri uyu Mudugudu, ngo nyuma yo gukora iperereza bawujyana mu Bitaro bya Kabgayi.

Iradukunda Emmanuel we yahise atabwa muri yombi.

Aya makuru yanemejwe n’Umuvugizi wa Polisi mu Ntara y’Amajyepfo, CIP Hassan Kamanzi avuga ko uriya musore afungiye kuri sitasiyo ya Polisi ya Muhanga.

Yavuze ko Polisi yibutsa urubyiruko gukura amaboko mu mufuka rugakora, rukirinda amakimbirana arimo ibyaha byo gukubita no gukomeretsa kuko bigize icyaha.

CIP Hassan Kamanzi yavuze ko gushaka icyabateza imbere ari byo bizafasha urubyiruko kubaho neza mu mahoro, no gutera imbere.

Six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second largest city, on Saturday.

Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows about a dozen people running inside two buildings before a black car with its front window open passes, followed by a police car.

Another video shows the moment that gunshots were heard in the city's main market square.

Poland's interior minister described the suspect - a 25-year-old Polish citizen - as being inspired by "far-right ideologies"; police said he used "military weapons" in the attack.

Hours after the attack, Polish PM Donald Tusk said three other bodies were found at the suspect's home, which is still being searched.

Nyuma yo kuzana ubuzima bwe bwite mu Itangazamakuru, Hossam Hassan wari umutoza w’ikipe y’Igihugu ya Misiri [Les Pharaons], yamaze gusezererwa kuri izo nshingano, asimburwa na Ali Maher.

Ni iki cyatumye Hossam asezererwa kuri izi nshingano?

Kimwe mu byababaje ubuyobozi bw’Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru mu Misiri, ni uburyo uyu mutoza yashyize ubuzima bwe bwite mu Itangazamakuru. Muri uyu mwaka, yatandukanye n’abagore be babiri bari barasezeranye.

Nyuma yo gutandukana n’aba bagore, Hossam Hassan yahise ashaka uwa Gatatu kandi byose byabaye muri uyu mwaka.

Nyuma yo gutandukana n’abahoze ari abagore be, hatangiye amakimbirane nabo ndetse bijya mu bitangazamakuru yaba iby’iwabo n’ibindi mpuzamahanga. Uku kugirana amakimbirane, byatumye ubuzima bw’umuryango w’uyu mutoza.

Hassan yasabwe gutuza ariko biramunanira!

Nyyma y’uku gukomeza gushyamirana n’abahoze ari abagore be, Ishyirahamwe ry’umupira w’amaguru muri Misiri ryamusabye kureka gushyira ubuzima bwe bwite ku ka rubanda, ahubwo umutima we akawerekeza ku ikipe y’Igihugu aho gukomeza kujya mu mpaka zerekeye ubuzima bwe bwite.

Ntabwo byamukundiye kuko ahubwo byageze aho hagaragaraga amafoto y’urukozasoni agaragaza abari abagore be. Imiryango Iharanira Uburenganzira bw’Abagore yo muri iki gihugu, yahise ihagurukira kwamagana ayo mahano.

Abakinnyi ba ‘Les Pharaons’ bababajwe n’ibyabaye kuri uyu mutoza!

Ibi byose byakomeje kugaragara mu Itangazamakuru, byababaje abarimo abakinnyi b’ikipe y’igihugu, ndetse bamwe mu bayikiniye banenga uko uyu mutoza akomeje kugaragara mu itangazamakuru.

Abakoresha be bamubujije kujya mu Itangazamakuru ariko biranga!

Hossam Hassan yahagaritswe ku kugaragara mu biganiro cyangwa gutanga ibitekerezo ku bitangazamakuru ariko uyu mutoza kubireka bikomeza kumugora.

Nyuma y’aho, Ishyirahamwe ry’umupira w’amaguru muri iki gihugu ryafashe icyemezo cyo gutandukana na we, asimburwa na Ali Maher.

Hossam yari yahawe akazi mu 2024 ariko ubwo yavaga mu Gikombe cy’Isi 2026, yongererwa amasezerano yagombaga kuzageza mu 2030.

Ubwo Misiri iheruka mu Gikombe cy’Isi, yasezerewe igeze muri 1/8 itsinzwe na Argentine nyuma yo gutsindwa ibitego 3-2.

Long ruling Benjamin Netanyahu is almost getting dislodged from Israel’s top office by election challenger Gadi Eisenkot.

Gadi Eisenkot will get the first attempt at forming a new government, putting him a step closer to flushing out Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Gadi Eisenkot is a former General in the Israel Army. He secured more support from the incoming Knesset than current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but not enough to secure a majority.

President Isaac Herzog announced Saturday evening that he would task Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israel’s next government.

Eisenkot will formally receive the mandate at a ceremony at the President’s Residence on Sunday at 5 p.m.

He will then have 28 days to form a government, with Herzog authorized to grant him an extension of up to 14 days if necessary.

If he fails, Netanyahu could next be given the chance to do so.

Eisenkot said in a post on X that “now is the time for the formation of a national emergency government,” adding: “I will do everything to make us worthy.”

He served from 2015 to 2019 as the 21st chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and from 2023 to 2024 as a minister without portfolio in Israel’s unity government.

He is also the leader of the Yashar party.

He led Yashar in the 2026 Israeli legislative election as the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

He is now the Prime Minister Elect of Israel starting from 8 November 2026.

Taarifa Congo Desk has established that the battle hardened FRN Rebels conducted a blistering offensive against Congolese troops and effectively seized strategic towns of Kalonge and Bitale in South Kivu Province.

Eyewitnesses narrated to a local radio station that the rebels entered Bitale on Saturday morning.

“RFN elements are in Bitale. They overran through a place called Masanganjiya and are in Bitale,” a local source said.

The outgunned Congolese troops with Wazalendo militia fled to Myowe village. The government forces are still present in Bulambika.

The FRN rebels have also gained control of Kalonge, another agglomeration in the Kahuzi Biega National Park.

“They have been here since 4:30 p.m. FRN soldiers are visible in Fendula, specifically at the group leader’s house,” the same source said.

Local sources indicate that FRN rebels who captured Kalonge passed through Kabare, Mudaka, Biega, Kasurusiru, Fendula.

The day before, clashes were widespread on several fronts, in several territories of the province of South Kivu, including Kabare, Kalehe, Fizi, Mwenga and Walungu.

Inzego z'ubutungane muri Irani zashize mu ngiro igihano c'urupfu caciriwe abantu batatu bari bafashwe mu gihe c'imyiyerekano yabereye mu gisagara ca Karaj muri Nzero (1), nk'uko vyatangajwe n'itororokanirizo ry'amakuru Mizan rifitaniye isano n'ubutungane muri ico gihugu.

Abanyonzwe ni abitwa: Hassan Deoband, Hamid Kazemi na Reza Zanganeh.

Nk'uko itororokanirizo Mizan ribivuga, uko ari batatu bagiriwe n'icaha co gukorana na Israel hamwe na Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika mu bijanye n'umutekano, hamwe no mu kwitwaza ibirwanisho mu myiyerekano yabaye ku magenekerezo ya 8 na 9 Nzero (1), uno mwaka. Baragirijwe kandi kugira uruhara mu gusambura no guturira inyubakwa rusangi hamwe n'ibikorwa remezo vy'umuyagankuba.

Iryo tororokanirizo rivuga ko ivyo bihano vy'urupfu vyashizwe mu ngiro ku musi w'Imana, inyuma y'uko vyemejwe na Sentare nkuru ya Irani. Amatungo yabo agiye kwigarurirwa na reta nk'uko vyategetswe n'iyo sentare nyene.

Mizan ryongeyeko ko hari n'abandi bantu 10 batawe muri yompi ku bijanye n'urwo rubanza, mu gihe abandi baciriwe ibihano vyo gupfungwa biri hagati y'imyaka itanu na cumi.

Mohamed Salah has scored 10 goals in 15 games for Turkish club Trabzonspor

Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans.

That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers after the expiry of his Liverpool contract , he asked one of his entourage what he should wear.

"The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too.

From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown.

"I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us."

Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him.

At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else.

Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival.

"Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel.

The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier.

Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival.

On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg.

"He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud.

At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million.

Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination.

The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions.

Trabzonspor trail leaders Galatasaray by three points, having won seven of their first 10 games, including victories against the table-toppers and Besiktas.

For context, the Istanbul 'big three' of Galatasaray (26), Fenerbahce (19) and Besiktas (16) have won the league on 61 occasions combined, compared with Trabzonspor's seven titles.

"In Turkey, he is the biggest football star after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo," says Kerim Tonyali, who is part of Gurbetci Gencler, a Trabzonspor supporters' group.

And given Salah's status as an icon, Trabzonspor are quickly becoming the second club for many in Turkey and the wider Muslim world.

Salah's face is a common sight wherever you go in Trabzon

Trabzon may be more than 2,000 miles from Liverpool but there are similarities, particularly when it comes to the sense of identity and pride associated with originating from here.

"Everywhere is Trabzon for us," is the local mantra and aligns with the sense of unity within this city that has a population of about 800,000 and is only the 30th-biggest in Turkey.

For Salah, the financials were important and he is earning about £14.6m per year as well as 20% of official merchandise sold with his name on, but one of the key aspects of coming here was the ability to focus entirely on his football.

Besiktas was considered as an option after the 2026 World Cup but, after multiple calls with Trabzonspor, Salah felt they were the ideal fit and offered a life away from the hustle and bustle of Istanbul.

He has his own security detail and is living in the nearby town of Yomra, where he now has a street named after him. He also employs a private chef and, unsurprisingly, continues to set standards in the gym and on the training ground.

By all accounts, Salah is thriving. He is a fan of Turkish coffee and is often spotted leaving the ground with Ayran - a traditional yogurt drink - but as much as he wants to explore the city, he knows of the difficulties given his reputation.

"Everyone wants to work with a star like Mohamed Salah," said Trabzonspor's Paul Onuachu, formerly of Southampton. "He adds so much and helps all of us and he contributes positively. I am grateful for him. It's a blessing to play with him."

Watching Salah in the flesh in a Conference League game against Freiburg, his pace has gone down a notch compared with his peak but the touch, quick feet and sheer quality is still there. And so is that knack of getting in goalscoring positions, even if his defensive duties - which were such a source of debate last season at Liverpool - are limited.

Salah believes he still has plenty to give for club and country, with aspirations to play in both the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations and 2030 World Cup, which will be partly held in North Africa.

No decision has been made about how long he will stay in Turkey, but there is growing belief among sources in the Middle East that he will move to Saudi Arabia when his two-year Trabzonspor deal expires in 2028. By then, he will be 36.

Salah signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor in the summer of 2026

On initial thoughts, it is easy to question how and why Salah ended up here.

When he delivered that infamous mixed-zone interview at Leeds ' Elland Road less than a year ago and the wheels of his departure from Liverpool were set in motion, surely no-one would have imagined his next destination would be this Turkish outpost near the Georgian border.

"I remember looking at him when we landed in Trabzon and seeing the crowds outside and how emotional it was," says Anil Dincer, one of the lawyers involved in Salah's move to Turkey.

"We already have Salah and Fabinho. So now we are waiting for [Virgil] Van Dijk," adds Serhat Sumer, a Trabzonspor fan.

Salah, of course, delivered so much joy to Liverpool and the intention here is the same. This is no drift towards retirement, but a player determined to prove he still belongs at the highest level and that football still has meaning beyond trophies and money.

Asked by BBC Sport if he had a message for Liverpool fans, Salah simply said "hello" and smiled. Given how rarely he spoke in the mixed zone during his time at Anfield, it is not in his nature to talk regularly on record.

Last season was Salah's least prolific at Anfield, but given Liverpool 's struggles in front of goal in the Premier League, it is hard to argue they have replaced one of their greatest ever players.

Perhaps a time will come when the likes of Salah, Arne Slot and Richard Hughes will reveal more about the chain of events that led to the forward agreeing to terminate his contract a year early. As it is, none of them are at the club and that chapter is firmly closed.

Salah's influence that once helped shape the Premier League is now being felt on the shores of the Black Sea. He is Trabzonspor's force of nature. And the team known as the Black Sea Storm are rising and on the hunt for silverware with their Egyptian King.

Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year

Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge.

Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips.

In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row.

And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner.

The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup.

Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville.

They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.

The North Pennines National Landscape aimed to mitigate climate change related flooding

Climate change readiness and helping people access the countryside are among priorities in a five-year plan for a national landscape.

The North Pennines National Landscape Management Plan 2026-31 has been adopted by the Cumberland, Westmorland and Furness, County Durham and Northumberland councils.

Work to ensure the North Pennines was "as prepared as possible for future climate challenges" included restoring peatland to help reduce flooding and equipping farmers with wildfire fighting equipment such as drones.

Chris Woodley-Stewart, director of the North Pennines National Landscape (NPNL), said: "In many ways, its the most ambitious plan that we've ever had, but also the most realistic."

National landscapes were formerly known as areas of outstanding natural beauty, and the North Pennines features heather moors, dales, woods and one of England's highest waterfalls High Force.

NPNL is mainly funded by the government and other charitable organisations.

One of the priorities in its management plan announced last month was adapting to "warmer, wetter winters and hotter, drier summers".

The area is home to High Force waterfall

NPNL said uplands were "especially vulnerable to the effects of climate change" through rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and increased frequency of extreme weather events.

Mitigation work like protecting existing woodlands and restoring carbon-rich peat soils would help safeguard upland ecosystems but also support downstream communities by "improving water quality and reducing flooding", it said.

One of the area's largest land managers, Raby Estates, said it worked with NPNL on wildfire prevention measures including managing its farmers' fuel loads and providing firefighting equipment.

Duncan Peake, chief executive at Raby Estates, said drone equipment to help spot fires was a "really significant, additional tool in our wildfire control kit".

As part of the management plan, NPNL said it was would also work with farmers who wanted to get the skills and equipment for farm visits.

Peake said farmers on their estate were already taking groups of mostly young people "who wouldn't normally have an opportunity to come to the countryside" to help them understand how farming works.

Woodley-Stewart said: "You can't make people come to the countryside and invest in the local economy, but you can help to create circumstances in which they feel this landscape is for everybody."

He said the five-year plan would guide the policy of the local authorities but would not be compulsory.

"There's no stick here, it's all carrot," Woodley-Stewart said, adding: "Everyone has a role to play in its implementation."

Seagrass is often described as the sea's equivalent of a woodland

More than 430 seagrass shoots have been discovered in the Fowey Estuary, giving conservationists hope that one of the UK's most important marine habitats can be brought back to Cornwall's waters.

The new growth was recorded across 50 patches of seabed during summer surveys carried out by Cornwall Wildlife Trust.

The findings come despite fears the restoration trial might not succeed when only six seedlings had emerged by the end of April.

Chloe James, of Cornwall Wildlife Trust, said the shoots were "hugely encouraging" after an "uncertain start to the spring".

Volunteers collected seagrass seeds from a donor meadow in Torpoint in autumn 2025 before planting them in the estuary. The seeds remained buried through the winter before beginning to grow in spring.

Volunteers have been collecting and planting thousands of seeds

"The new growth is a powerful reminder of why restoration work takes time, persistence and a willingness to keep learning," said James.

The project is part of Seeding Change Together, a partnership between Cornwall Wildlife Trust and Seasalt Cornwall that began in 2022 .

Earlier work involved some of the trust's first attempts to restore seagrass meadows in Cornwall's estuaries, with volunteers collecting and planting thousands of seeds while researchers tested different restoration methods.

More seeds are due to be planted in the Fowey Estuary and Helford Estuary

Seagrass, which may not look remarkable, is often described as the sea's equivalent of a woodland, said the trust.

It provides shelter and nursery grounds for fish and other marine life, helps improve water quality, locks away carbon and reduces coastal erosion.

The trust said mainland Britain had lost up to 92% of its seagrass meadows over the last century. Previous research highlighted by the project found seagrass could capture carbon up to 35 times faster than tropical rainforests.

The restoration effort has not been without setbacks. In the Helford Estuary, algal growth appeared to wipe out planted seedlings at one site, although three plants were later found to have survived and had started spreading.

More seeds are due to be planted in the Fowey Estuary and Helford Estuary, with further monitoring planned for spring 2027.

Iyo umuntu agiye kurondera canke kuraba intare mw'ishamba, ikibanza ca mbere aba yiteze kuzisangamwo ni hasi, mu bisaka, musi y'ibiti. Ariko, mu karere k'ikiyaga ca Manyara muri Tanzaniya no mw'ishamba rya Ishasha muri Uganda, hari izimaze kugira inyifato itamenyerewe, aho zisigaye ziruhukira mu bushorishori bw'ibiti.

Iyo uzihweje uri kure, wokwibaza ko ari utuyabu turyamye twitekaniye. Ariko mu vy'ukuri ziba ari intare nini kandi zikomeye. Ziba ziriko zihweza iryo shamba mu mutekano nta ngere, ibitangaza cane ingenzi nyinshi ziba ziteze kuzisanga hasi mu vyatsi canke mu bisaka.

Muri rusangi, intare zifatwa nk'ibikoko biganza ibiyaya binini. Imibiri yazo y'inguvu kandi ifise imitsi ikomeye yaremwe ku buryo zishobora guhiga inyamaswa zifungura zikayirukako, zigendera hasi, gushika ziyifashe.

Ugereranije n'ingwe hamwe n'inguge, intare ntizwi cane nk'iyifise ubuhinga bwo kwurira ibiti. Ingwe n'inkende zo zifise imibiri itaremereye cane, kandi zirashobora kugenda no gutaruka ziva kw'ishami ry'igiti rimwe zija ku rindi. Ivyo bituma zishobora kumara umwanya muri ivyo biti ata ngorane.

Ariko rero, mu turere tumwe two muri Afrika yo mu Buseruko, intare zaragize inyifato idasanzwe. Zisigaye zurira ibiti zikamara n'umwanya munini ziri hejuru mu mashami yavyo. Iyo nyifato itangaza abashakashatsi, ndetse igakwega n'ingenzi hamwe n'abakunzi b'inyamaswa zo mw'ishamba.

Mu vy'ukuri, muri ayo mashamba, intare zarahinduye cane ingeso zari zisanzwe zifise. Birashika ukabona imirwi yazo iruhukiye ku mashami manini y'ibiti, aho zimara amasaha menshi mu gihe c'ubushuhe bwinshi bwo ku murango.

Abahinga mu vy'inyamaswa zo mw'ishamba bavuga ko kwurira ibiti ari bumwe mu buryo izo ntare zikoresha kugira ngo zimenyere canke zitahure neza ishamba zibamwo.

Iyo imvura itasuye mu kiyaya ca Rift, ivyatsi birebire bica bihinduka ubuhungiro bw'udukoko turyana, harimwo n'isazi zinunuza amaraso y'izindi nyamaswa. Iyo ziruhukiye mu biti, intare ziraronka akayaga kazifasha kugabanya ububabare n'ukutoroherwa ziterwa n'utwo dukoko.

Ikindi, ku murango, isi irashuha cane kubera imishwarara y'izuba. Mu biti ho, haba hari igitutu n'akayaga gahoraho, haba hakanye cane. Ivyo biha intare ahantu heza ho kuruhukira, bigatuma umubiri wazo udasesagura inguvu zitari ngombwa mu kugerageza guhangana n'ubushuhe.

Uretse ko ibiti bizikingira ubushuhe n'udukoko, iyo izo ntare ziri hejuru ku biti, biranazifasha kubona neza agahita irya n'ino. Zirashobora kubona bitagoranye ahaherereye ubusho bw'imbogo, bw'impongo, n'ibindi bikoko, uko bigenda vyegera aho birisha canke ahari ivyambu vy'amazi. Ivyo birazifasha gukurikirana no guhiga ico zifuza gufata.

N'ubwo intare zishobora kumara umwanya mu biti, ntizishobora kuvyurira neza nk'ingwe. Ingwe zifise umubiri muto kandi muremure, hamwe n'umurizo muremure uzifasha kutajugumba iyo ziri hejuru ku mashami y'ibiti. Intare zo, zirasumba cane ingwe mu bunini no mu buremere, ivyo bigatuma kwurira ibiti bizigora.

Rimwe rimwe, iyo intare ziri hejuru ku mashami y'ibiti, zirakoroka. Ico ni ikindi gitangaza kandi kigakwega ingenzi ziba zifise amahirwe yo kukibona.

Ariko, ukwo gukoroka ntikuzica intege cane. Muri make, zifise ubushobozi budasanzwe bwo kwihanganira ingorane. Kenshi zica zivyuka, zikikunkumura umukungugu uziri ku mubiri, zigaca zisubira kwurira ca giti nyene kugira ngo zisubire aho zisanzwe ziruhukira, nk'uko womengo nta cari cabaye.

Fabian Hurzeler got St Pauli promoted to the Bundesliga before leaving for Brighton in June 2024

"We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge," were Fabian Hurzeler's words as Brighton exited the Carabao Cup at the hands of Manchester City .

The following Saturday, the 33-year-old's dogged defiance manifested in a 1-0 victory over the same opponents, who failed to score at home for the first time in 23 matches.

Brighton now sit in third place, only behind City and Premier League leaders Arsenal , both teams they have beaten this season.

And they have done so with a bravery and front-footedness that the likes of Arsenal and City have not always been used to facing.

Brighton's front-footedness has enabled them to win the ball back proactively, quickly turning moments of defence into attack

With 24 goals in nine games, Brighton are the league's top scorers but it is their defensive work that has underpinned their underdog victories against the league's best teams.

Notably, Brighton have conceded just seven goals this season - with only Arsenal conceding fewer.

From opposition goal-kicks, Brighton look to press high and in a man-to-man fashion. This is a common approach but Brighton 's intensity across the pitch makes them better at executing this than most.

The challenge is that the opposition will have an extra player in their build-up compared to Brighton 's 10 pressing outfielders, if they use their keeper as a passing option.

That potential issue is managed by one of Brighton 's attackers leaving the centre-back they began marking - curving their run as they press the opposition keeper.

In curving their run, the aim is to cut off the passing angle back to they player they are no longer marking, while the rest of the team are responsible for their direct, individual opponents.

Charalampos Kostoulas first presses Gabriel Magalhaes before curving his run to press David Raya. This cuts off the pass back to Gabriel. The rest of the Brighton players are applying pressure in a man-to-man fashion.

Kostoulas' pressure on Raya forces him to kick the ball out of play early in the game

In spite of generally opting to play man-to-man across the pitch, at points in their build-up the team in possession may have an unmarked player.

This player is usually in an area of the pitch that is hard for them to access - such as their full-back or winger on the far side.

This is often an intentional decision Brighton take, believing the benefit of an extra pressing player closer to the ball is greater than the risk associated with leaving that opposing player unmarked.

By ensuring the opposing unmarked player is far from the ball, they reduce the likelihood that player is found. By putting more bodies around the ball, they increase the likelihood of winning the ball back.

Maxim de Cuyper curves his run as he presses Gianluigi Donnarumma. This makes it hard for City's keeper to pass it to Abdukodir Khusanov. With the angle to City's right side cut off, Brighton also leave Matheus Nunes, the far-side full-back, unmarked, knowing that finding him is difficult. Down City's left, they press man-to-man

What makes Brighton so unique though is how they defend deeper.

Most teams who press high from opposition goal-kicks then settle into a more rigid defensive shape closer to their own goal. These defensive blocks are generally examples of zonal defending rather than man-to-man defending.

The most common defensive block for top teams tends to come in the form of a 4-4-2. Players are tasked with marshalling specific 'zones', aiming to make it harder for opponents to get into dangerous positions. There is often a focus on blocking the centre of the pitch, with the wider areas less congested for opponents to play in.

Brighton 's magic this season is in the form of continuing to use man-to-man ideas, albeit in a more measured fashion, when pushed closer to their own goal.

This more measured version of a man-to-man press is seen in Brighton 's use of an extra player, or a 'plus-one' (+1) in their backline. Put simply, if opponents commit four forwards high up the pitch, Brighton will defend with five.

As such, Brighton aren't looking to go man-to-man everywhere, always, but they are looking to do it as much as they can while adhering to two key principles: trying to keep a plus-one in defence and while focusing on blocking the centre of the pitch.

In this example, we see almost every one of Brighton's defensive principles in one move. Here we see Brighton take a man-to-man approach from a deeper starting position

As Martin Odegaard dribbles deeper, Chema Andres, who began marking him, leaves the Arsenal captain to move back into midfield, providing central cover. As much as Brighton want to apply man-to-man pressure, they are also wary not to be pulled across the pitch in a way that leaves gaps in dangerous areas

In yellow, we see Brighton's man-to-man references in defence. In white, we see Brighton's spare player in defence. In blue, we see Chema, taking a more conservative, zonal defensive position, protecting the middle of the pitch

As Odegaard steps into a more dangerous position, Chema engages with him once again. Brighton are man-to-man across the pitch, while staying centrally compact. The only exception to their man-to-man defence here is the deliberately spare player at centre-back, Luka Vuskovic, highlighted in white

Odegaard passes the ball to Declan Rice, who is pressed by Yasin Ayari. Rice plays the ball into Kai Havertz, who is pressed by his respective marker stepping out of a centre-back position. Havertz is forced to play the ball back to Ezri Konsa

These ideas were seen clearly against Manchester City too.

In possession, Enzo Maresca asked right-back Matheus Nunes to push up and move infield, into a position that resembled a right-sided striker.

City, as well as the likes of Paris St-Germain and Arsenal , have used their full-backs in these unorthodox attacking positions as it poses difficult questions to the opponent who tracks them.

These players tend to find space as opposing wingers are typically less willing to track an attacking full-back all the way into their own box.

Hurzeler has used Maxim de Cuyper as his left winger this season, but the Belgian has played the majority of his career at left-back. This has equipped him with the work-rate and defensive nous to deal with the modern, roaming attacking full-back.

In man-to-man fashion, De Cuyper followed Nunes all the way into his fixed position higher up the pitch, and ended up defending at left centre-back - as Brighton created a back five. When Brighton had the ball, De Cuyper was back playing at left wing.

De Cuyper, Brighton's left winger, has tracked Nunes, City's right-back. This results in a Brighton back five. In white, we see Brighton's 'plus-one' player

Remember Brighton keeping a +1 at the back? Naturally, this leaves the other team with a spare player somewhere else. It is usually one of the opposition centre-backs who remain unmarked, finding themselves with time and space on the ball.

In an ideal situation, a centre-back less confident on the ball would be a good candidate to leave unmarked.

But even for impressive ball-playing defenders, the challenge is that every player they could pass to remains marked or could become marked in a fraction of a second based on how Brighton set-up.

Brighton are also continually shifting, looking to find moments in which one player can spring to press the unmarked centre-back on the ball. When this jump happens, Brighton will lock on to a full man-to-man press, looking to force a turnover or push the opposition back towards their keeper.

Ayari turns to notice Bruno Guimaraes' position

De Cuyper turns to notice Jurrien Timber, free at right-back. These looks help the Brighton players organise their man-oriented press

De Cuyper's attention is drawn to Timber. Pascal Gross presses Rice and Ayari is blocking the pass into Guimaraes. The pass back to Konsa triggers Ayari to step up on to Rice as Gross applies pressure to the previously unmarked Konsa

This ends up looking like a vertical domino effect across the pitch. Chema then steps up from a holding midfield position to press Guimaraes. Brighton have ended up man-to-man around the ball

There are solutions to this organised yet man-oriented defending and Abdukodir Khusanov's powerful ball-carrying from a wider position was perhaps the best Manchester City had on show.

But combining key principles in the form of blocking the centre of the pitch and not being baited into mindlessly tracking players looking to stretch their shape, while still locking on to individual players nearby, make Brighton an incredibly difficult puzzle for teams to solve.

For as potent as they have been in attack, it is their bravery in defence that has given them the platform.

Cray Wanderers, one of the four oldest clubs in England, are playing in their 78th FA Cup campaign this season

If at first you do not succeed, try and try again. And again. Until, at the 78th attempt, you finally make it.

Formed in 1860, Cray Wanderers are one of the oldest football clubs in the world - and the oldest club in London still in existence.

And yet the Wands had never reached the FA Cup first round in their 166-year history.

It was perhaps fitting that Cray only just scraped through in the fourth qualifying round against Bedford Town in dramatic fashion to achieve something they have tried and failed to do 77 times before.

Following a 0-0 draw on 17 October away at Bedford, it was back to Flamingo Park for a replay three days later.

The game ended 1-1 after 90 minutes and went to extra time.

Bedford then took the lead in the 101st minute, only for Cray striker Ade Yusuff - who has scored in all four rounds so far - to make it 2-2 and force a penalty shootout.

Wands goalkeeper JJ Briggs, who is on loan from Cambridge United, made two saves in the shootout to help pave the way for history to be made in Chislehurst.

When teenager Jakob Lowe stuck away his effort from 12 yards to seal a 4-3 win on penalties, the scale of the moment was not lost on club captain Frankie Raymond.

Cray Wanderers midfielder and captain Frankie Raymond, right, says qualifying for the FA Cup first round is a "great occasion" for the club

"It means a massive amount to us all," Raymond told BBC London.

"It's a club steeped in history and to be the first set of players and staff to take the club to the first round is a massive achievement for everyone."

Raymond is right about the remarkable history at Cray.

From helping to form the Kent League in 1894 and serving as a nursery club to Woolwich Arsenal - known today simply as Arsenal - between 1895 and 1907, much has gone before in this little pocket of south-east London.

And in more recent times, the Cray Wanderers youth setup is where it all started for Manchester City and England centre-back Marc Guehi at the age of six.

BBC to show Cray Wanderers v Stockport & Altrincham v Notts County

England's Marc Guehi makes me so proud - ex-coach

Cray are 18th in the Isthmian League Premier Division - the seventh tier of the English football pyramid.

Tim O'Shea's side are only outside the relegation zone on goal difference, although they do have at least four games in hand on the teams around them.

The journey to the FA Cup first round has been far from simple for the Wands, with three replays required in the four qualifying rounds, meaning they have played seven matches - with 660 minutes of football - to make their dream a reality.

And their reward for getting this far? One of the hardest draws possible at this stage of the competition.

They will host League One's second-placed team Stockport County, live on BBC Two on Sunday (14:15 GMT).

FA Cup first round: Cray Wanderers v Stockport County

Ex-Hornchurch and Folkestone Invicta striker Ade Yusuff has scored 11 goals in all competitions for Cray Wanderers so far this season

For Cray's top goalscorer Yusuff, Friday will be spent in the school classroom where he works as a teacher before his attentions turn to the biggest game in the club's history at the weekend.

The school corridors have been full of "really excited" pupils chatting about the upcoming encounter against the Hatters, the 32-year-old said.

"They're really looking forward to it, they're really proud," Yusuff added.

Despite Stockport being 112 league positions higher than Cray, Yusuff hopes he can keep his cup goalscoring run going.

"I don't see why not," he said. "The team are in really good form and when the boys are creating chances the way they are, I always back myself - no matter who it's against - to score."

Yusuff also believes they can cause an upset, having already knocked out National League South side Maidstone United and National League North team Bedford.

"I think it's all about momentum," he said. "We've beaten higher teams in different positions in the earlier rounds. I think it's about believing in ourselves.

"A lot of the boys here have really good careers ahead of them. They have to have these occasions and these moments so they can say: 'I can do it and I can achieve something myself'."

Mark Hunt has been following Cray Wanderers since 2010

Someone else who refuses to rule out a giant-killing is Cray Wanderers fan Mark Hunt.

"Anything could happen," he said. "There's always a David and Goliath story. We had one last year when Macclesfield beat Crystal Palace.

"There's a big, big gap between Macclesfield and Palace. Why can't it be Stockport v Cray?

"Most people expect the underdogs to fail, most times they will, but a few slip through the net.

"You get one shot at it. And the fact it goes straight to a penalty shootout, no replay, no VAR, artificial pitch - it could go in our favour."

Attendances at Flamingo Park fluctuate between 130 and 900, but Sunday's tie with Stockport sold out in five minutes, with 2,500 fans expected.

"It means the world," added Hunt. "It's been such a long time coming. It's something we've been waiting for for so long, just to get a shot at a Stockport County.

"It's going to be an incredible occasion."

Amerika yatangaje ko izotanga ingero ishika ku miliyoni 20 z'amadolari ku muntu wese azoyironsa amakuru ajanye n'umugambi wa niklyere wa Irani.

Urwego rwa reta ya Amerika rujejwe gutanga ubushimwe ku batanga amakuru mwene ayo, ruvuga kandi ko rushobora gufasha kwimurira mu kindi gihugu umuntu azotanga ayo makuru.

Perezida wa Amerika, Donald Trump, yari yatangaje mu mwaka uheze ko ibibanza vya Irani bikorerwamwo ivyerekeye inguvu za nikleyere vyasambuwe burundu, inyuma y'ibitero vy'indege Amerika na Israel zagavye kuri ico gihugu.

Irani iguma isigura ko porogarama yayo ari iya nikleyere y'amahoro gusa, kandi ko ata mugambi ifise wo gukora ibirwanisho ruhonyanganda.

Hagati aho, igisirikare ca Amerika kivuga ko kiriko kirashiraho umurwi udasanzwe ujejwe gukomeza utwigoro twa Washington two kubuza Irani gucisha ku mbibe zayo ibirwanisho hamwe n'ibikoresho vyafatiwe ibihano.

Bumwe mu buyobozi bwa gisirikare bwa Amerika bwitwa CENTCOM, bwavuze ko umurwi udasanzwe witwa 'Task Force Iron Gate' uzokorera mu gisagara ca Tampa, muri reta ya Florida, ukazokorana n'izindi nzego za reta ya Amerika.

Uretse gukurikirana uruja n'uruza rw'ibirwanisho, uwo murwi uzokwibanda kandi ku kurwanya no kuzibira ibikoresho bishobora gukoreshwa mu bikorwa vya gisirikare no mu bikorwa vya gisivire, hamwe n'uburyo butemewe bwo kwinjiza amafaranga.

CENTCOM ivuga ko ibihano vyo mu mazi yashize ku bivuko vya Irani vyatumye ico gihugu kidashobora gushora hanze ibitoro vy'agaciro karenga imiliyaridi 25 z'amadolari y'Amerika.
